title: Separably generated and separable field extensions (not necessarily algebraic)
statement: Let $K/k$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. For a family $(x_i)_{i\in I}$ of elements of $K$ let $k(x_i;i\in I)\subseteq K$ be the subfield generated by $k$ and the $x_i$. (1) $K$ is *separably generated over $k$* if there is a transcendence basis $(x_i)_{i\in I}$ of $K/k$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis] such that the extension $K/k(x_i;i\in I)$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], i.e. the minimal polynomial over $k(x_i;i\in I)$ of every element of $K$ is separable (coprime to its derivative). (2) $K$ is *separable over $k$* if for every subextension $k\subset K'\subset K$ with $K'$ finitely generated as a field over $k$ (that is, $K'=k(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ for finitely many $a_1,\dots,a_n\in K$), the extension $K'/k$ is separably generated in the sense of (1).

proof.text: (The notions used in (1).) For the field extension $K/k$, a transcendence basis $(x_i)_{i\in I}$ is defined in [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis] (Stacks 030E (4): algebraically independent over $k$, with $K/k(x_i;i\in I)$ algebraic), and $k(x_i;i\in I)$ is a subfield of $K$ containing $k$, so $K$ is a field extension of $k(x_i;i\in I)$ [def-pc-field-extension] and the condition 'separable algebraic' of [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] applies to it. Its algebraicity half holds already by the definition of a transcendence basis, so (1) only adds that every $\alpha\in K$ is separable over $k(x_i;i\in I)$. Stacks writes $k(x_i;i\in I)$ for the fraction field of the polynomial ring (030E (2)); for an algebraically independent family $k[X_i]\to K$ is injective, so it extends to an injective map of the fraction field onto the subfield generated by the $x_i$, and the two readings agree. Clause (1) asks for the existence of one such basis; it does not need that transcendence bases exist (Stacks Fields Lemma 030F, Mathlib `exists_isTranscendenceBasis`), so no further statement is used.

source.place: Algebra, Definition Tag 030O (definition-separable-field-extension, line 9915) (1); Fields Definition Tag 030E (definition-transcendence, line 3369) (2), (4); Fields Definition Tag 09H1 (definition-separable, line 1165)

proof.text: (Agreement of 'separable' with the other notions of the DAG.) Stacks Fields 09H1 (1) calls an irreducible polynomial separable if it is relatively prime to its derivative; [def-pc-separable-polynomial] says the same for any polynomial, and the minimal polynomial is irreducible, so 'the minimal polynomial is separable' means the same under both. Some nodes (def-weil-pbc-relative-separable-closure, lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points) call $\alpha$ separable over $F$ when it is a root of some separable $f\in F[T]$; this is the same: if $f(\alpha)=0$ with $Uf+Vf'=1$, the minimal polynomial $P$ divides $f$, say $f=PG$, so $f'=P'G+PG'$ and $(UG+VG')P+(VG)P'=1$, hence $P$ is separable; conversely take $f=P$. The Fields chapter's restatement 030J (2) ('an algebraic extension $k'/k$ is separable if every element is separable') is the same definition. So the notion 'separable algebraic' used in (1) is unambiguous.

source.place: Fields, Definition Tag 09H1 (definition-separable, line 1165) and Definition Tag 030J (definition-separable-algebraic, line 3723); divisibility argument written by the agent

proof.text: (The subextensions in (2).) For finitely many $a_1,\dots,a_n\in K$, $K'=k(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ is the smallest subfield of $K$ containing $k$ and the $a_j$; it contains $k$, so $K'/k$ is a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] and (1) applies to it, with transcendence bases taken inside $K'$. 'Finitely generated over $k$' in Stacks means generated as a field by finitely many elements, which is this. Hence (2) is a well-formed condition on $K/k$.

(What the definition does not contain.) Stacks remarks right after 030O that it is not clear from the definition that a separably generated extension is separable; this is Algebra Lemma 030X (lemma-separably-generated-separable, line 10410), and Lemma 030P (lemma-subextensions-are-separable) says subextensions of separable extensions are separable. Neither is part of the definition or used in steps 1-3; they are statements about this node and are not created here (no node cites them yet). Note the clash of words: for an algebraic extension, 'separable over $k$' in the sense of (2) is meant to agree with 'separable algebraic' (Fields 09H1 footnote), but that agreement is also a lemma and not used here; nodes citing this node mean (2). The characteristic-zero case is lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-separable, which depends on this node.
